chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the fasting person if his eye aches, does he apply kohl with radish or similar things, or is it permissible for him to do so? He said, 'He does not apply kohl.'

key_terms.بِالذَّرُورِ: with radish (a common medicinal substance used for kohl)

ai.seo_question: Does applying medicinal kohl break the fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a specific legal ruling for a fasting person suffering from an eye ailment, instructing them not to apply medicinal kohl (ithmid). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic debate on whether substances reaching the brain via the eye's optic nerve invalidate the fast, with 'la yaktahil' often interpreted as a prohibition to avoid doubt or as an indication that it breaks the fast depending on the school of thought. The context underscores the practical application of *fiqh al-sawm* in daily health matters, emphasizing caution in maintaining the spiritual integrity of the fast during illness.
